title: Research: seed 51 P120 shared-total diagonal obstruction (no new kappa)
body:
## Change

Adds a finite exact audit of the calibrated C.6 two-target, one-shared-extra-total decoder ansatz on the full P120 E8 line set for the seed-selected pencil `e=L_51`, `d0=L_1`.

The exhaustive replay considers all 120 targets and 511 nonzero nine-bit sink labels. It finds 27 calibrated rows and 351 distinct-target pairs. Every pair makes the union of required extra sources available at both sinks, but every pair places both targets in the other row's required-source set. The resulting shared total cancels both relaxed diagonals, so there are no exact pairs in this family.

This is a scoped negative result only. It does not cover uncalibrated rows, other pencils, other correction mechanisms, or complete suppliers, and it claims no new `kappa`.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/p120-calibrated-two-target-seed51/verify.py
```

Expected leading line: `PASS_P120_CALIBRATED_TWO_TARGET_SEED51`.

The replay validates the 120 root and label certificates, checks the full 112-by-112 P112 C.6 witness as a positive control, and runs root/label mutation controls. Package metadata and exact source pins also pass. Local Python is 3.14.7; Python 3.12 is unavailable here, so the repository's registered Python 3.12 replay remains for CI.

## Provenance and overlap

Base commit: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. `SOURCES.json` pins the task card and predecessor source blobs. This extends Douglas R. Colkitt's `c6_asym.py` mechanism and Mason Ellerbroek's `e8units.py` construction; the P112 control recovers targets 75/76, sinks 329/438, and 24 shared sources.

I refreshed the complete open-PR and discussion snapshot before submission. Adjacent masked-decoder work includes P112 component/one-entry audits and P104 local-rigidity work; the P120 A8-simplex obstruction uses a different decoder family. No direct overlap was found for this fixed-pencil shared-total claim.

Contributor: Cinna Davis. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used for search design, exact replay implementation, proof explanation, and packaging.
